ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $D$ and $E$ are the midpoints of sides $AB$ and $AC$ of $\triangle ABC$, respectively. If $DE = 12$, what is the length of $BC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: Since $D$ and $E$ are the midpoints of sides $AB$ and $AC$ of $\triangle ABC$ respectively, \\
it follows that $DE$ is the midline of $\triangle ABC$, \\
hence $BC = 2DE$, \\
since $DE = 12$, \\
it follows that $BC = \boxed{24}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, and C is at the lower right. Point D is on side AB, point E is on side AC, and line segment DE connects D and E and crosses the triangle horizontally, looking parallel to base BC. The problem text gives that D and E are respectively the midpoints of AB and AC, and DE=12. Reasoning: Because D and E are respectively the midpoints of the two sides AB and AC of triangle ABC, DE is the midline of triangle ABC. According to the triangle midline theorem, DE is parallel to BC, and the length of DE is equal to half of BC, that is, DE=BC/2. Therefore BC=2×DE=2×12=24.
